1.explanation: We’ve set up ESLint exactly as in the bug report: using Babel-ESLint, the React plugin, and `key-spacing` in multiLine align:'value' mode. The test component has an inline style object that originally lives on one line. When you run `eslint --fix`, ESLint will break that object into multiple lines (because of the `object-curly-newline` and `object-property-newline` rules) and then apply the key-spacing alignment algorithm. In JSX the rule doesn’t account for the surrounding braces correctly, leading to the extra spaces before certain property values and mis-positioned closing braces. This reproduces the “ugly” formatting shown in the screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: When you use ESLint’s `key-spacing` rule with `{ multiLine: { align: 'value' } }` together with the React plugin, and you have a JSX attribute whose value is an object literal with multiple properties on one line (for example, an inline `style`), running `eslint --fix` will split the object into multiple lines and then try to horizontally align the _values_ of all its properties. In JSX this leads to incorrect extra padding (spaces) before some values, mis‐placed braces, and generally “ugly” formatting, as shown in the screenshots.
